To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the estrogenic quinone 3,4-oestrone-quinone (3,4-E2Q) is genotoxic to human breast cancer cells and that the genotoxicity of 3, 4-E2Q is mediated by the formation of ss DNA breaks.
3,4-o-estrone-quinone (3,4-E0) is a potent inducer of single-strand (ssDNA) breaks in human breast cancer cells (MCF-7), and the ssDNA breaks are partially repaired after a 2-h recovery period.

the DNA damage induced in MCF- 7 cells by the quinone analogue 3,4 estrone-o-quinones (3,4-Eq) is qualitatively and partially quantitatively similar to that of estradiol-quinone (Eq) and that 3,4 EQ-induced ss DNA breaks are not mediated via the topoisomerases, estrogen receptor or the B ring of the estradiol molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and quantitation of the DNA lesions formed in human cells exposed to a metabolite of estradiol.
the DNA damage induced by an estrogen metabolite, 3,4-o-quinone (3,4-E), in a human breast cell line.
the DNA damage induced by the quinone analogue of estrone, 1,5(10)-estradiol-3,4-quinone, in human cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
3,4,7,8-estratriene-3,17-diol-3,4-epoxide, a known carcinogen, is not a major metabolite of 17beta-estradiol in vivo.
3,4,estrone-o- quinone, a metabolite of estrone, induces ss DNA breaks in a human breast cell line, MCF-7, in the absence of the estrogen receptor.
3,4-o-quinone, an estrone metabolite, can induce ss DNA breaks, which are partially repaired, in human MCF-7 breast cancer cells and BT-20 breast cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3,4-o-quinone, a metabolite of the procarcinogen estrone, induces ss DNA breaks in human breast cancer cell lines.

the ss DNA damage induced by the estrogen metabolite 3,4-Q is not mediated via the ER or topoisomerase II, and the A and B rings are the essential components of 3, 4-EQ required for the formation of ss DNA damage.
the DNA damage induced by estrogen metabolites, such as 3,4-Q and 4-hydroxyestrone (4-OHE2), is mediated by the quinone moiety of the estrogen metabolite.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ss DNA breaks are the primary DNA lesions induced by 3.4-EQ in human cells.
the DNA damage induced by the 3,4-o-quinone of estrone is not likely to be estrogen receptor-mediated and is not likely to involve DNA cross-links, intercalation or topoisomerase inhibition.
the 3,4-o-quinone metabolite of estradiol, 3,4-eq, is able to produce ss DNA damage in estrogen receptor-positive and estrogen receptor-negative human breast cancer cells.
